label: conj:cl3-zeta5-geometric-realization
title: Geometric realisation of $\mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5)$ as a Bring-natural depth-3 invariant
html:
Conjecture. Geometric realisation of \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) as a Bring-natural depth-3 invariant

Conjecture (geometric realisation of the depth-3 Bring trilog \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) — candidates list).

The depth-3 canonical witness conj:bring-trilog-depth-3-witness established that

  \mathrm{Cl}_3\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{5}\right) \;=\; \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5)
  \;=\; 0.18936791501083168387944480476641361363127422974423\ldots

is a depth-3 grouplike value of \mathcal{H}_q at the S_5-Bring-natural input \zeta_5 — i.e. an element of \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2 in Goncharov's period filtration. Open question: which geometric or topological invariant realises this number on the archimedean side?

Three candidate identifications, in order of plausibility

Candidate 1: hyperbolic 4-manifold volume on a Bring-natural cusped quotient

Goncharov (1995, 2002) and Beilinson–Levin connect \mathrm{Li}_3 values at algebraic points to volumes of hyperbolic 4-manifolds via the regulator K_5^{\mathrm{ind}}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R}/\pi^4 \mathbb{Q}. A specific 4-manifold is needed:

  • Cusped 4-mfd with S_5-cuspidal monodromy. Compactified moduli space \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,5}/S_5 — a 2-dim complex, 4-dim real space — has cusps shaped on the S_5-orbit of \zeta_5. Its hyperbolic volume should be a \mathbb{Q}-linear combination of \{\mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi a/5) : \gcd(a, 5) = 1\} values.

Discharge target: identify the specific 4-manifold and its \mathbb{Q}-coefficient in \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5).

Candidate 2: Chern–Simons of an icosahedrally-symmetric knot in S^3

The icosahedral group A_5 \subset S_5 acts on \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) with three orbits of size 12, 20, 30 (the icosahedral configuration). Knots whose holonomy representation lands in this A_5-orbit have Chern–Simons invariants whose archimedean evaluation involves \mathrm{Li}_3 at \zeta_5 shape parameters.

Specifically, for a hyperbolic knot K with shape parameters in \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5), the complexified volume

  \mathrm{CS}(K) + i\,\mathrm{Vol}(K) \;\in\; \mathbb{C} / \pi^2 \mathbb{Z}

has imaginary part (volume) at depth 2 and real part (CS) at depth 3. For an A_5-symmetric knot, the depth-3 part should be expressible via \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) and its Galois conjugates.

Discharge target: identify a knot K with \mathrm{CS}(K) \stackrel{?}{=} \alpha \cdot \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) + \beta \cdot \zeta(3) + \cdots for explicit \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{Q}.

[!WARNING] Update (canonical refutation): A PSLQ canonical experiment on the CS invariants of the seven Bring-natural torus-knot generators \{T(2, 3), T(2, 5), T(2, 7), T(2, 9), T(3, 4), T(3, 5), T(5, 2)\} reveals that their Chern-Simons invariants are exactly rational (e.g., \mathrm{CS}(T(2,5)) = 1/20, \mathrm{CS}(T(2,3)) = -1/12). Therefore, their CS invariants cannot be expressed as non-trivial \mathbb{Q}-linear combinations of transcendental numbers like \zeta(3) and \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5). This strictly rules out torus knots as direct geometric realisations for this depth-3 period under Candidate 2.

Candidate 3: iterated integral on \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0, 5}

Goncharov's motivic fundamental groupoid of \mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0, 1, \infty\} generalises to \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0, 5}, the moduli of 5 ordered marked points on \mathbb{P}^1. Iterated integrals there generate weight-3 multiple polylogs at 5th-root-of-unity values; specifically, at the S_5-orbit of base points, the integrals realise

  \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5),\; \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^2),\;
  \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^3),\; \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^4) \;\in\; \mathcal{P}_3.

Discharge target: write down the explicit iterated integral \int_\gamma \omega on \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0, 5} whose period evaluates to \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) for the right contour \gamma and form \omega.

Comparison: all three candidates are conjecturally equivalent

The three candidates above are conjecturally the same mathematical content viewed through three lenses:

  • Candidate 1 (hyperbolic 4-mfd volume) is the geometric image of the Beilinson regulator on K_5^{\mathrm{ind}}.
  • Candidate 2 (knot CS) is the dual / complementary image at the 3-mfd level — same regulator in a different basis.
  • Candidate 3 (iterated integral) is the motivic source — both Candidates 1 and 2 are special evaluations of it.

The geometric realisation question is then: which is the canonical representative for the QOU paper's purposes? Candidate 2 is the most directly compatible with the existing knot-theoretic framework; Candidate 1 is the cleanest from the period-theoretic side; Candidate 3 is most general.

Consequences of an explicit identification

Identifying any one of the three candidates explicitly would:

  1. Close the depth-3 row of the depth correspondence. The correspondence (conj:gb-depth-period-correspondence) currently has the figure-8 row at depth 2 verified and the trilog canonical witness at depth 3, but no geometric image for the trilog value. Identification would make the depth-3 prediction as concrete as the depth-2 prediction.
  2. Test joint-action commutativity at depth 3. The Galois action on \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) via \zeta_5 \mapsto \zeta_5^a should match the action on the geometric side (4-mfd cusps, knot CS, or marked-point permutations) — a sharp test of conj:joint-galois-braid-action.
  3. Provide the Bring-natural depth-3 witness target. The witness formalism (the canonical formalism) currently records the algebraic value; geometric identification would let it record a measurement target (e.g. SnapPy CS computation on a specific knot) and verify equality at 50 dps.
